confirmed: Client type-5 packet has four serialized arguments: FString-like at client rbx (RVA 0x03484F25), local [rbp+0x10] (0x03484F35), custom identity path [r13+0x160] (0x03484F48), local [rbp+0x20] (0x03484F58).
Server candidate block deserializes to [r14+0x1A0], [r14+0x1B8], local [rbp-0x70] through the custom path, and local [rsp+0x60] in that order.
Server code immediately examines field #2 [r14+0x1B8], scans '?' (0x3F) and '#' (0x23), and routes it through URL/structured-string helpers at RVAs 0x0368B200, 0x036B4720, and 0x014086E3E0.
findings.candidate: Field #2 (client [rbp+0x10] / server [r14+0x1B8]) is the strongest URL/options-shaped candidate from delimiter parsing, but LoginOptions identity is not proved. Existing findings label field #1 as RequestURL and leave field #2 unnamed; no field may be selected for grant injection.

confirmed: Client constructs an FOutBunch at RVA 0x03484ED2 through 0x031CF3D0, writes type 5 at 0x03484EDE, calls serializer with rcx=&[rbp+0x90] at 0x03484F25/35/48/58, then sends through connection vtable +0x2C8 at 0x03484F76; this callsite is outgoing/save by dataflow.

Serializer RVA 0x0189D040 has a branch on archive byte [rcx+0x28] bit 0. The taken branch consumes a signed length from archive storage and writes bytes into the destination FString-shaped object; the other branch reads source length/data and writes length/bytes through archive vtable +0x150. These are load/save dataflow branches.
Server login-shaped block at 0x036CE317 uses incoming archive rsi and writes four decoded destinations; this is the corresponding load-side dataflow.
unproven: The native symbolic name/meaning of the archive flag byte and the runtime branch value at each NMT callsite were not dynamically observed.

confirmed: Client local [rbp+0x20] is released by 0x018E5490 at 0x03484FA1 and local [rbp+0x10] is released by the same helper at 0x03484FAF after the send.
Serializer temporary buffers are released through 0x018E5490 at 0x0189D2B1, 0x0189D41C, and 0x0189D5FB on relevant paths.
Serializer mutates/reserves destination fields and writes terminators; it is not a read-only borrowed-view operation.
unproven: Exact FString allocator, capacity invariant, ownership transfer, and whether any callsite field is safe to replace with a borrowed view remain unproven. A borrowed injection would risk the observed release path.

confirmed: Current findings identify server RVA 0x036CDCE0 case 5 as reading RequestURL, a second FString, Unique ID, and a final FString in that order.
